note: Shipping thresholds live HERE, in one place, not baked into profession records. Professions that fail are flagged ship:false, never deleted — a flag can be rendered as a delete, a delete cannot be rendered as a flag. Change a number here and re-run tools/export_csv.py to re-derive every shipping block.

compensation_filter.rule: CUT if mid_career_midpoint < 4.5 LPA, OR (mid_career_midpoint < 6.0 AND ai_exposure.band == 'high')
rationale: Why an absolute ceiling and not the payback ratio: payback does not discriminate. Every profession except Commercial Pilot repays in under 2.5 years, and the TRADES have the best ratios in the dataset — Mason repays in 0.09 years while trapping you at 3.0 LPA for life. Ranking by payback would put masons first. Payback is kept as a capital-risk FLAG, not a filter.

Why 4.5 and not 5.0: at 5.0 the cut takes Welder, which has AI exposure 7 — the most future-proof career in the dataset. Also HVAC and Solar Technician, both growing. Deleting the safest careers over 50,000 rupees a year is the wrong trade.
Why 4.5 and not 4.0: 4.0 at 5-8 years of experience is barely above an IT fresher salary. A career still paying that after 8 years is a trap.

Why the AI clause exists: a pure pay filter keeps Website & Online Store Builder at exactly 4.5 despite exposure 77 — low pay in a job that is actively disappearing. The clause also correctly SPARES Software Tester (7.5) and Data Analyst (9.0), which are high-exposure but pay enough that entering via the automation track is rational.

regional_note: 4.5 LPA is calibrated for urban and metro India. In tier-3 and rural districts the same figure supports a materially different standard of living. This is the main reason failing professions are retained rather than deleted — a regional threshold can be applied later only if the data still exists.
known_limitations: Wage figures come from commercial salary aggregators (Indeed, Glassdoor, salary sites), not government data. India has no authoritative free source for occupational earnings.
Automobile Mechanic fails at 4.2 but EV servicing is genuinely lifting demand. Flagged for revisit.
mid_career EXCLUDES business ownership by design. A plumber running a contracting firm earns well, but the earning attribute there is entrepreneurship (Sector 5), not plumbing.
